clue.text: A playboy of this world finds a sweet, dizzy registered nurse, a short one!

definitions.note: the clue alludes to Synge's play The Playboy of the Western World; 'this world' stands for the adjective

indicators.note: a dizzy head spins, so these letters are whirled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
RN is the short form of registered nurse

explanation.surface: A man about town discovers a sweet, scatterbrained little nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the title of J. M. Synge's play The Playboy of the Western World: the playboy is of the world the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synge's comedy is titled The Playboy of the Western World, so the playboy's world is the occidental one.

clue.text: They were famous tumblers.

parts.note: suggests a celebrated troupe of performers
reads as acrobats, but means things that tumbled down

explanation.walkthrough: Tumblers look like acrobats; the answer is the biblical city walls that fell at Joshua's trumpets.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Joshua the city's fortifications collapsed when the Israelites blew trumpets and shouted.

clue.text: You? Me? Him? Her?

parts.note: reads as a question about who is meant
every one of these pronouns names a single unspecified person

explanation.walkthrough: The four questions are each candidates for an unnamed individual: the answer covers any of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an unspecified person, which any of the pronouns could be.

clue.text: Force 2 to leave, and bad vice will end up at the crossroads.

definitions.note: 2 is the answer to 2 Down, someone

indicators.note: the jumbled vice finishes at the crossroads letter, which comes last
bad here means spoiled, so the letters of vice are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
the letter T is shaped like a road junction

explanation.surface: A moral warning: make that person go, for wickedness ends at the crossroads.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 means the answer to 2 Down: the definition reads 'force someone to leave'.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who expels a tenant by legal process turns them out of their home.

clue.text: It's regular after dark, but it sounds more like King Arthur's round table!

indicators.note: the answer said aloud is the same as a word describing the knights

parts.note: the Round Table was the company of Arthur's knights, so it is knightly

explanation.surface: Something happens every evening but seems fit for Camelot.
explanation.walkthrough: The K of the knightly word is silent, so both words are spoken alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done every night happens regularly once darkness falls.

clue.text: Our former president, in short, dined on a primary color, as silk might be, or livestock.

definitions.text: as silk might be, or livestock

parts.note: W is the nickname of George W. Bush, the former US president
to dine is to eat, past tense ate
red is one of the primary colours

explanation.surface: A potted biography: an ex-president once ate something red, like silk or cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: W ('Dubya') is a common American shorthand for George W. Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Watered silk has a wavy moiré finish, and livestock are watered when given drink.

clue.text: When you're at this, you've had it up to here and don't know what to do or which way to turn–but it sounds like you've lost your sense of humor!

definitions.text: When you're at this, you've had it up to here and don't know what to do or which way to turn
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the idiom for utter exasperation

definitions.text: you've lost your sense of humor
definitions.meaning: second meaning, heard literally: your wit has come to its end

explanation.surface: A sympathetic description of exasperation that ends with a joke about humourlessness.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'at your wit's end' is heard literally: the end of your wit, the faculty of humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a loss with no idea how to cope is the idiom of exhausted mental resources.

clue.text: It's a toss-up–lose on purpose or pitch it?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a toss or cast
second meaning: deliberately lose a contest

explanation.walkthrough: Three senses of one word: a toss, deliberately losing a game, and pitching a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed match is one a side lets go deliberately, and a baseball pitcher hurls the ball.

clue.text: Idolizes the silversmith and his family?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: holds in deep respect
second meaning: the family of Paul Revere, the Boston silversmith and patriot

explanation.walkthrough: Paul Revere, famous for his midnight ride of 1775, was a Boston silversmith.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate someone is to worship them; Paul Revere's household would be the Reveres.

clue.text: Crazy Theodore's sister, commonly, stops–just ceases…

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Ted is the short form of Theodore, with its 's
sis is the casual, common form of sister

explanation.surface: Mad Teddy's sister, as people call her, simply quits.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave off an action is to discontinue it, so the verb means halts or ceases.

clue.text: Little devil in a little fish! But it could keep you off-kilter.

definitions.note: a gerund used as a noun, matching the answer

indicators.note: the devil is placed in the fish, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: the ling is a fish of the cod family
an imp is a small mischievous devil

explanation.surface: A tiny demon hidden in a small fish might throw you off balance.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking with an uneven gait from injury leaves a person lopsided and unsteady.

clue.text: Blossom and more! Three's around four if you miss the point.

indicators.note: the shortened Three's goes around four, enclosing it
a compass point, East, is dropped from the word

parts.note: the word three with its 's, read as letters
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A garden boast followed by a puzzling bit of arithmetic about threes and fours.
explanation.walkthrough: The point is a compass point: E (East) comes out of THREE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish and prosper is to blossom, and the answer suggests growing even beyond that.

clue.text: Fire the mechanism, or go all out?

parts.note: to fire a gun is to shoot
taken as written
the works of a clock or machine are its mechanism

explanation.surface: A gunsmith's question: trigger the mechanism, or spend everything?
explanation.definitionFit: The American idiom means to risk or spend everything at once, holding nothing back.

clue.text: See 11
See 11
No toll here! A wee fry, stirred, makes it perfect.

definitions.note: a cryptic way of saying a road that charges nothing

indicators.note: a stirred mixture is jumbled, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook's tip: stir a tiny fry-up and you get it just right.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as a road that is free: in the US, freeways usually carry no toll, unlike turnpikes.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeway is an American highway, typically without tolls, so the road is free to use.

clue.text: …while little Theodore existed, switched, and got thinner and thinner until he almost disappeared!

definitions.text: got thinner and thinner until he almost disappeared

indicators.note: the two pieces swap places, so the existing word comes before the name

parts.note: existed is past tense of be: was
Ted is the short form of Theodore

explanation.surface: Teddy's story goes on from the previous clue: he lived, changed, and faded away.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads Ted then was; switched swaps them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has wasted away has grown emaciated, losing flesh through illness or hunger.

clue.text: Hates the exams, I hear.

indicators.note: the setter is reporting what is heard, so the spoken phrase gives the answer

parts.note: exams are tests, so this is the phrase 'the tests'

explanation.surface: A student's grumble: someone loathes the examinations.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something is to loathe it strongly, a direct synonym of hating.

clue.text: See 15
What the mechanic does to the car could mean a certain fellow has reached the top of the beanstalk!

definitions.text: What the mechanic does to the car
definitions.meaning: first meaning: raises the car on a jack

definitions.text: a certain fellow has reached the top of the beanstalk
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Jack is up, as in the fairy tale Jack and the Beanstalk

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as Jack's up: the hero of the fairy tale has climbed his beanstalk.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic lifts a car with a jack; and the climber of the beanstalk in the fairy tale is named Jack.

clue.text: See 1
The 6 stops here, but he's part of the nine, with Tom dear in Paris.

definitions.text: The 6 stops here, but he's part of the nine

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: A baseball scene: the pitch is stopped by one of the team, joined by Tom and his French sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is the answer to 6 Down, throw; the nine is a baseball team.
explanation.definitionFit: On a baseball team of nine players, the catcher crouches behind home plate to stop the pitcher's throws.

clue.text: Choose Junior! If one does this to others, it is bullying.

definitions.text: If one does this to others, it is bullying

parts.note: to choose is to pick
Junior is the son who shares his father's name

explanation.surface: A parent's choice of the youngest child, which other children would call bullying.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeatedly singling out others for unkind treatment is the idiom for harassing them.

clue.text: Walking along to add a heavy weight here to name a London station.

indicators.note: the clue says the answer needs a weight added, so the station is the answer plus that weight
adding the weight to this answer names the station, so taking it away leaves the answer

parts.note: Paddington is a major railway terminus in London
a ton is a large unit of weight

explanation.surface: Directions while strolling: add something heavy and you reach a London railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is worked backwards: the answer plus a ton spells the station, so the station minus the ton is the answer. Paddington is a London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: To pad is to walk softly and steadily, so padding is walking along.

clue.text: The prisoner of war has a point–communist!–and has specified fuel.

parts.note: POW is the standard abbreviation for prisoner of war
E (East) is a compass point
red is the traditional colour of communism, so a communist is a red

explanation.surface: A captured soldier has a point to make, is a communist, and has fuel to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine described as gas- or steam-driven runs on the stated energy source.

clue.text: Uncle, I'd badly gather relevant parts to comprise.

indicators.note: something done badly is muddled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An uncle's clumsy attempt to round up the right bits for a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To contain as parts of a whole is to take something in as a component.

clue.text: Gee, I hear escorts showing those who exclaim fulsomely, or just "Well, well, well."

definitions.text: those who exclaim fulsomely, or just "Well, well, well."

indicators.note: the setter is reporting a sound, so the word gee gives the letter it sounds like

parts.note: said aloud, gee is the letter G
ushers escort people to their seats

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the sight of escorts and talks effusively.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition has two halves: effusive talkers, and oil wells that spout, hence 'well' three times.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gushes speaks with excessive enthusiasm; a gushing oil strike is a free-flowing well.

clue.text: Confused stare makes these of interest.

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled, so the word stare is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled look turns out to be the thing that intrigues people.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the definition as 'these' in the phrase '___ of interest'.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks charge and pay interest at stated percentages, called interest rates.

clue.text: Beat it! State animal!

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: An exclamation followed by a state's official creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang commands telling someone to go away at once.

clue.text: Boss! The number comes before an exclamation of pain.

indicators.note: the number is placed ahead of the cry of pain in reading order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
ow! is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A worker reacts to the boss with a number and a yelp of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss is not the employer here: it is an old American farm word for a cow, as in 'bossy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boss, or bossy, is a traditional rural American name for a cow or calf.

clue.text: The angel does this for show, and reverses.

definitions.text: The angel does this for show
definitions.meaning: first meaning: an angel, a theatre investor, funds a production

explanation.walkthrough: An angel is a financial investor in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre angel supports a production with money; a car that reverses goes backwards.

clue.text: Blue? Goose? Straw? Rasp? Chuck?

parts.note: each word comes before the answer to make the name of a fruit
Chuck is the rock-and-roll pioneer whose surname completes the list

explanation.walkthrough: Each word combines with the answer: four fruits, then Chuck, the rock-and-roll guitarist of Johnny B. Goode.
explanation.definitionFit: Small juicy fruit names end in this word, and it is also the surname of rock guitarist Chuck.

clue.text: Birds of a feather? 11 is stirred with Royal Crown shortly to produce it.

indicators.note: the letters of 11's answer are stirred like a mixture, so they are jumbled

parts.note: the answer to 11 Across, the first light of the linked entry
shortly means just the initials of the two words are used

explanation.surface: A recipe for a flock: mix one clue's answer with a cola brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 refers to the first light of 11 Across, not the whole linked answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of a feather flock together, so the phrase means companions or close allies of one kind.

clue.text: Change of direction–or directions? Either way, it will be way different!

definitions.text: Change of direction–or directions? Either way, it will be way different!

parts.note: reads as a turn on a journey, but means a change to the directions given for the route
reads as slang for very different; it means the way taken will be another one

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is 'way different': slang for very different, but literally a different way.
explanation.definitionFit: To send traffic or a journey along another path is to alter its course and its directions.

clue.text: People having a row? It's just the same old crew.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people rowing a boat, not quarrelling
second meaning: the members of a boat's crew

explanation.walkthrough: Row looks like a quarrel and crew like a gang of familiar faces; both are boating.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers who pull the oars make up a boat's crew, and they are literally having a row.

clue.text: Suffering an eclipse, sundry northeast steamships briefly find arid conditions.

indicators.note: in an eclipse the sun is blotted out, so the sun is taken from the word sundry

parts.note: taken as written
SS is the prefix for a steamship, here for steamships

explanation.surface: During an eclipse, assorted ships off the northeast find a drought.
explanation.walkthrough: The eclipse hides the SUN inside 'sundry', not a sun in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of moisture is the state of being arid, so the conditions are dry ones.
